prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single universal “best” — the best interior painter for you depends on your home, budget, schedule, and expectations. I can help you find top-rated local options, but first here’s a quick plan so you pick the right contractor and get comparable bids.

How to find the best interior painting company in St. Louis
- Define priorities: price, speed, high-end finish, eco‑friendly paints, historic-home experience, warranty, etc.  
- Look in several places for candidates: Google Maps/Reviews, Yelp, Angi/HomeAdvisor, Houzz, BBB, Nextdoor, and local Facebook groups.  
- Verify each candidate: current insurance (liability and workers’ comp), business license if required, and local references or recent project photos.  
- Check reviews but read the details (how the company handled problems is more important than perfect 5‑stars). Ask for two or three references you can call.  
- Get at least 3 written estimates that list scope clearly (prep, number of coats, primer, paint brand/finish, trim/ceiling details, cleanup). Compare apples to apples.

What to ask every painter (quick checklist)
- Are you licensed/insured? Can I see proof?  
- Which paint brands and finishes do you use? Do you warranty your work? For how long?  
- Exactly what’s included in prep (patching, sanding, caulking, primer)?  
- How many coats will you apply to walls/trim/ceiling? Is primer included?  
- Timeline and start date, how many workers, estimated days on-site.  
- Cleanup, furniture moving, floor protection policy.  
- Payment schedule and contract terms (get everything in writing).

Typical price guidance (ballpark)
- Small bedroom: a few hundred dollars to ~$1,000 depending on prep and finishes.  
- Whole-house interior: commonly $2,000–$10,000+, highly dependent on size, trim detail, prep work, number of coats, and paint quality.  
(Prices vary widely — rely on written estimates.)

Red flags
- Asks for full payment up front.  
- No written contract or vague scope.  
- Extremely low bid with pressure to sign immediately.  
- No references or very recent negative reviews about communication or cleanup.

Want me to narrow it down?
If you give your zip code, project details (number of rooms, ceilings, trim, desired timeline, any problem areas like water damage), I can recommend how to find and compare top-rated St. Louis painters and help draft a message to request estimates.
